props.title: The Ugly Truth

sections.content: The Ugly Truth exemplifies the late 2000s romantic comedy formula, following the contentious relationship between uptight TV producer Abby (Katherine Heigl) and crass relationship expert Mike (Gerard Butler). It's a direct descendant of classic battle-of-the-sexes comedies like When Harry Met Sally (1989) and You've Got Mail (1998), but with raunchier humor reflecting the post-Apatow comedy landscape. The film's gender politics haven't aged well, echoing problematic elements from Knocked Up (2007) and 27 Dresses (2008).

sections.content: The film sits at an interesting crossroads in rom-com history. By 2009, the genre was moving away from the polished Nora Ephron style of Sleepless in Seattle (1993) toward more provocative territory. Films like Friends with Benefits (2011) and No Strings Attached (2011) would soon push boundaries further, while maintaining the core romantic comedy structure. The Ugly Truth attempts to bridge this gap, mixing traditional rom-com beats with edgier content. SUBHEAD: Evolution of Modern Rom-Coms

The late 2000s marked a transitional period where romantic comedies struggled to stay relevant. While The Ugly Truth aimed for broader appeal with its mix of classic and contemporary elements, films like (500) Days of Summer (2009) were actively deconstructing genre tropes. This evolution continued with Crazy, Stupid, Love (2011) and Silver Linings Playbook (2012), which brought more complex character development and nuanced relationships to the format.
